title: timed-regional-shedder-with-transparent-slo-deescalation-and-auditlog
author: Ananya Kapoor
release_notes: Add a timed, SLO-aware token shedder that performs controlled regional failovers after a configurable cooldown; includes an audit log for circuit state transitions and new telemetry for per-tenant shed events. Backwards-compatible; defaults off for private installs.
description:
Motivation: After INC-2026-007 we observed cascading tenant failures when short-lived regional congestion caused long-lived circuit states and immediate full failovers. This PR implements a timed SLO-aware shedder that applies conservative token-level shedding for tenants approaching soft-SLO violation windows, and only triggers regional failover after a configurable cooldown and a transparent de-escalation period. The implementation also emits an immutable audit trail of circuit transitions so ops can reconstruct decisions after the fact.

What this PR changes (high level):
- New component: timed_shedder (pkg/serving/shedder) — evaluates tenant SLO error/latency windows and issues token-shed directives that the router applies as a per-tenant rate cap.
- Failover gating: a cooldown timer + quorum check prevents an immediate region-wide failover; only after the cooldown and persistent SLO breach we mark routes sticky-failover.
- Transparent de-escalation: when pressure subsides we decay shed allowances over a configurable window so callers see progressive capacity restoration rather than abrupt jumps.
- Audit logging: auditlog.go captures immutable JSON events for: shed_start, shed_update, failover_initiated, failover_aborted, deescalation_start, deescalation_complete. Events include tenant_id, reason, metrics_snapshot, and operator_request if present.
- Telemetry: new metrics for shed_rate, shed_duration, failover_cooldown_hits and per-tenant shed counters; integrated into metrics_registry.
- Tests: added e2e chaos yaml + deterministic integration test to validate cooldown gating and de-escalation semantics.

Backwards compatibility and rollout:
- Feature gated under runtime flag --enable-timed-shedder (defaults to false in private deploy values.yaml). Hosted will enable behind a canary rollout (10% traffic on dedicated pool first).
- No changes to public API. Router honors shed directives as a soft token cap so clients see throttling responses (503 with Retry-After) when their shed allowance is exhausted.

CI notes: initial run had a lint failure on auditlog.go; fixed by trimming long comments and reformatting JSON schema (2nd run passed). e2e took longer in Windows runners — test timeout tuned. Final CI status: pass.

Operational runbook excerpt (included in PR):
- Enabling: flip enableTimedShedder in values.yaml and set canaryTrafficPercent. Monitor shed_rate and failover_cooldown_hits for the first 15 minutes.
- Abort: set enableTimedShedder=false and post an operator action with abort reason. Use console handler /api/operator/shed-events to retrieve last 1k audit events.
- Rollback: Helm rollback will disable feature; ensure Kafka sink is drained before rollback to avoid duplicate audit lines.
